title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. 383-387 of this section): Grothendieck is computing explicitly with a group scheme G_{ρ,σ}, with variants G*_{ρ,σ}, SG_{ρ,σ} and SG°_{ρ,σ}, attached to the pair of elliptic orders (ρ,σ); the relevant case is presumably ρ=2, σ=3 for (P)SL(2,Z). Its elements are written as systems (α, β, μ, ε): α is a point of a torus T_ρ, β a point of N'_σ, μ a multiplier and ε a sign in μ_2. On the previous page he checked, via the parametrisation α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}, that the group law matches formulas (28). This rests on the isomorphism G_{ρ,σ} ≃ B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ, with coordinates (u, a, b).

This page is a side remark ('Notons à cette occasion').
(1) The systems (31) (α, β, 1, 1), with α and β sections of μ_2 (i.e. ±1), lie in SG°_{ρ,σ}. A bracketed justification says that SG° is stable under multiplying α, β by sections of μ_2, since this does not change the derived quantities α~, β~. A crossed-out line shows he first doubted this ('but non des SG...').
(2) Under the isomorphism above these systems correspond to (u, a, b) with u = 1 and a, b roots of unity (sign sections).
(3) They form a subgroup, the 'trivial sections' μ_2 × μ_2 of SG_{ρ,σ}, and the group law on it is ordinary componentwise multiplication.
(4) Translation by this subgroup on G*_{ρ,σ} is just multiplication of the α and β components by signs. Hence working with α, β 'defined only up to sign' amounts to working in the quotient G*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ_0, or SG*_{ρ,σ}(Ẑ)/Σ_0, where Σ_0 ≃ Z/2 × Z/2 is the subgroup of elements (α, β, 1, 1) with α, β ∈ {±1}.

Purpose: to make rigorous the habitual sign ambiguity in the local (inertia/torus) components of elements of the Grothendieck–Teichmüller-type group acting on the tower M_{0,3}^{!~}, M_{1,1}. This is essentially the passage between SL2-level and PSL2-level data, where the centre ±1 causes the ambiguity.
errors: No substantive error. One step is only asserted: that Σ_0 is a subgroup of G* compatible with the group law (normal, or central, so that the quotient is a group). This follows easily if the signs are central in the components, but it is not written out.

The inserted marginal formula '(α, β^3, μ, ε)' is unclear and does not obviously fit the argument. Similarly, 'Γμ_m' versus 'Γ(μ_2)' or 'Γ(G_m)' is ambiguous in the image. Read literally as G_m, the description of the (u,a,b)-image would be too large: it should be signs.

ideas.what: Subgroup Σ_0 ≃ Z/2×Z/2 of sign elements (±1, ±1, 1, 1); working with the local components α, β up to sign equals passing to the quotient group by Σ_0
ideas.modern_name: Quotient by the central sign subgroup (the SL2 vs PSL2 / ±1 ambiguity in GT-type groups and their local inertia data)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Standard; sign ambiguities in GT-hat are handled by Drinfeld (1990) and Ihara (1991)

ideas.what: Description of G_{ρ,σ} as B'_0 × T_ρ × T_σ via (u, a, b), with α = u a^{-1}, β = u b^{-1}
ideas.modern_name: Explicit coordinates on a group scheme of local (torus-valued) data attached to elliptic points
ideas.usually_credited_to: Unsure; no direct published counterpart known

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine bookkeeping remark: the sign elements form a Klein four-subgroup, and 'up to sign' means passing to the quotient. It is part of a longer explicit computation with no new idea on this page.
transcription_corrections: Line 2: the image reads roughly 'α ∈ Γ(μ_2), β ∈ Γ(μ_2)' (subscript 2 partly overwritten); the crossed-out line is '[but non des SG_{ρ,σ} si αβ ∈ Γ(μ_2)]', and its last symbol is uncertain.
'a ∈ Γμ_m', 'b ∈ Γμ_m' and the subgroup '≃ μ_m × μ_m' look in the image like 'Γ(G_m)' or 'G_m × G_m' or 'μ_2'. Mathematically the intended meaning must be μ_2, i.e. signs.
'{+μ_2×μ_2+}' is written above the line as an insertion; 'des sections triviales' is in quotation marks.

'Cela montre que le fait de travailler avec des α, β définis seulement au signe près revient simplement à travailler dans les groupes quotients...': the transcription has 'des travailler' and is missing 'à'.
